replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
I think he's trying to suggest now that the regular in-game player count should only apply to non-donors; that is, non-donors that join a game increase the displayed player capacity, while donors do not (or are logged under a separate head count). That way, people who are unable to join a full game won't have the option of requesting a generous donor to temporarily free a slot for them because donors, who have the ability to join even after the capacity is reached, are tallied discretely. Hopefully this isn't getting too confusing.

Nonetheless, there's some logic to it, as donors wouldn't ever have to make room for another player, only to rejoin and raise the player count over the limit. If the non-donor had simply arrived at the game first and taken the last spot, it would've had the same outcome. What was stated in the original post of the thread was that there should be a rule requiring donors to, essentially, sacrifice one of the perquisites of the rank they paid for — freedom of team selection. The very sound of it already leads to that it's a poorly developed idea, but that's not what the thread is about anymore.

This is way too many people. Also with premium members not affecting the player count, it will mean that it will be very hard to fill up a game full of non donors anyway, therefore essentially removing the premium perk. 

So overall I give this a -1. It's fine as it is.
